title: Sum That Never Overflows
statement: You are given n integers. Each one fits in a 32-bit int. Print the sum of all n integers. The sum can be far bigger than a 32-bit int can hold, so use a wider type such as long long for the total. Print only the sum.
inputFormat: The first line has the integer n. The second line has n integers separated by single spaces.
outputFormat: One integer: the sum of the n numbers.
constraints: The sum always fits in a 64-bit signed integer
explanations: Small numbers add up to 6. This is the simple case with no overflow.
Each number fits in an int, but four of them add up to 8000000000. That is more than a 32-bit int can hold, so the total needs long long.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = [int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n]]
    print(sum(nums))

main()
